source.title: 43-4051.00 - Customer Service Representatives
source.scope: The 2026 occupation page was consulted for communication, recordkeeping, billing, complaint referral, and work coordination. source.title: About native Support time duration metrics

source.scope: UK data-protection context for sufficient, relevant, purpose-limited information. The page explicitly says it is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act and may change. source.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams
source.scope: Context for impersonation, pressure, remote-access requests, and fake service or refund claims. The draft teaches reporting and approved contact routes, not scam scripts, credential collection, incident-response techniques, or universal payment-reversal rights.

source.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
source.scope: Occupational context for schedules, correspondence, records, office tools, supplies, and varied administrative roles. Legal, medical, and executive specialties have distinct preparation and responsibilities. No employment count is used as a curriculum-frequency claim, and this overview is not term-level review.

source.title: 43-6014.00 - Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
source.scope: The occupation-specific task overview was consulted for files, messages, calendars, meetings, documents, supplies, and travel coordination. Listed tasks are not universal permissions or a word-frequency ranking.

Current local schedules, holds, and authorized review still apply.

source.title: Hand Laborers and Material Movers
source.scope: Broad occupational context for manual movement, packing, stock, and order-filling work. source.title: Material Recording Clerks

source.title: Glossary of Legal Terms
source.publisher: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
source.scope: Selected passages consulted for affidavit, admissible, appeal/appellant, arbitration, file, jurisdiction, statute, subpoena, testimony, and transcript. U.S. federal context; this is not exhaustive term-level review or universal procedure. No deadlines, case strategy, response requirements, forms, or assets are adopted. Definitions in this course are original editorial drafts.

source.title: Confidentiality of client information
source.scope: Audience, confidentiality-versus-privilege, consent and authorized disclosure, information sharing, and support-staff context consulted. Updated June 30, 2022. Applies to SRA-regulated England and Wales practice. The source excludes specific data-protection rights, processing bases, and retention advice. Disclosure exceptions and safeguarding examples are not taught as permission or procedure. Linked Codes, cases, other guidance, and assets were not reviewed or acquired.

source.title: Court Records
source.publisher: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
source.scope: Overview body consulted for case files, dockets, documents, PACER access versus CM/ECF electronic filing, and record/access context. Linked registration, filing, access rules, fees, retention schedules, and forms were not read or adopted. The overview does not establish that all court records are public or that a record is complete or authentic. No assets acquired.

source.title: Civil Procedure Rules glossary
source.scope: Selected body passages consulted for affidavit, alternative dispute resolution, counterclaim, cross-examination, damages, injunction, limitation period, official copy, privilege, seal, service, set aside, stay, and without prejudice. The glossary guides existing meanings and does not create legal meaning. England and Wales civil context; the page displays January 30, 2017 update. Linked rules, forms, time calculations, legal validity assessments, and assets were not reviewed or adopted.

source.title: Leading question
source.scope: Entry body consulted for question wording that suggests an answer. Last reviewed June 2023. U.S. reference context; its permissibility discussion is not taught as a universal rule or questioning instruction. Linked Rule 611 and other entries were not opened. No source examples or assets are copied or acquired.

source.title: Circumstantial evidence
source.scope: Entry body consulted for support through inference rather than a direct account of the fact at issue. Last reviewed January 2022. U.S. reference context; the illustrative discrimination scenario is not copied or adopted, and no legal conclusion, proof threshold, or comparative weight is asserted. Linked entries and assets were not acquired.

source.title: Federal Rules of Evidence Rule 801
source.scope: Actual Rule 801(a)-(d) text consulted for statement, statement-maker, current trial or hearing, asserted-truth purpose, and the existence of exclusions. U.S. federal scope only. No admissibility determination, exception advice, advocacy method, or universal evidence rule is taught. Advisory notes and linked cases are not used as course evidence; no assets acquired.

source.title: Witnesses: Oaths, paragraphs 14-20
source.scope: Oaths paragraphs 14-20 consulted for the religious oath versus nonreligious affirmation distinction and respect for individual preference. England and Wales coroner context only. No age rule, ritual, prescribed wording, attendance process, or universal procedural requirement is taught. Linked legislation and guidance were not read, and no assets or quoted forms acquired.

review.draft_author: Codex retail_register_art (AI source consultation; not independent, human or specialist approval)
review.notes: Preserve two ordered current nouns: physical air-pocket bubble and wrapping-material wrap. Use the established reviewed Professional morph.wrap family observed in actual gift wrap; retain one exact word boundary and lowercase generic spelling. Professional morph.wrap intentionally remains broader than the chosen material role and admits its stored related action occurrences under inspection. This continues the accepted gift-wrap convention rather than asserting all noun/action meanings identical. review.draft_author: Codex retail_register_art (AI source consultation; not independent, human or specialist approval)
review.notes: Keep the existing whole borrowed packaging-box noun. The Professional sense usually uses cardboard but is not limited to food or drinks; actual Growth carton explicitly describes a cardboard food/drink container, so its narrower pair is inspected without silently broadening it. The two carton senses overlap in ordinary use; retaining separate current identities is conservative, not a claim of unrelated words. The source history points to paper-board vocabulary, not cart plus on. A reviewer may prefer a shared packaging core, but that would need an explicit scope decision.

The graph covers the stored general holding object; it does not approve freight specifications, software-container equivalence, food-contact use or any domain procedure.
